title: Was Jimmy really upset that Tommy killed Spider in Goodfellas (1990), given he was riling him up?

commenti.body:
You bring up a good point about Tommy and Jimmy about being as violent as each other, just different levels of control. But I think another factor is that Tommy’s violence is unpredictable as well as chaotic. 

The films sets up that he’s not above joking around with the “funny how?” scene. So I don’t think it’s out of the realm of possibility that Jimmy thought Tommy would pay no mind to a simple “go fuck yourself.” Maybe he thought he might hurt Spider but perhaps killing him was out of the question.

I think there’s a few things to consider here…

1) In the movie they had just gone through the Billy Batts ordeal, which included having to dig up his corpse and moving it elsewhere. It was a huge risk. Obviously Spider isn’t made or connected like Batts, but still a body to deal with and missing person that could come back to haunt them. Jimmy probably didn’t want to go through that again for no reason.

2) Killing Billy likely had some benefits for the crew. One less boss in the area to contend with. Risk-reward, which helps explain why Jimmy would participate. Killing Spider carries risk and accomplishes nothing.

3) I think it’s fair to assume Spider was well-liked. Spider worked for them, he obviously made the right connection somewhere, and he came back even after being shot. He also had the guts to talk back to Tommy. Jimmy surely knew violence was an option, but Tommy went straight for the kill, and now they’re down someone they trust.

4) Tommy killing Spider ruined their night. They were there to play cards and have fun, now they have to dispose of another body. He’s probably pissed that Tommy can’t control himself. 

5) Character-wise, Jimmy getting pissed reinforces his loyalty and code. Batts was a rival, but up until Lufthansa Jimmy never got violent with his own people. He’s the one who preached loyalty to Henry, he had no problem throwing money around to friends or to protect his interests (he even tipped Spider for the comment). After the heist though, the loyalty changes and his circle shrinks dramatically. It’s important for us to see after Batts that he’s not unhinged like Tommy (and it’s important for us to see that Henry isn’t like either).

It's also kinda interesting with the "funny how?" scene is that Tommy is getting entertainment from cruelty. He's letting Henry think that he might be in severe danger (given Tommy's volatility) just for his amusement, which is something a psychopath would do. It's almost just to demonstrate the power he has over people. To me it does the opposite of humanize him.

Jimmy is not saying "are you going to let him get away with that?" in a serious tone. He's joking, teasing, trying to the cut the tension of the situation, trying to get Tommy to kind of laugh it off. Guess it didn't work.
